title: Reduce visual thrash & CPU for timeseries: pixel-binning, legend inertia, and accessible tooltip exposure
creator: Maya Chen
description: Refactor time-series rendering behavior and interaction affordances to reduce CPU spend on long-range zooms and rapid scrubbing while improving legend/tooltip accessibility. Work includes: pixel-axis binning for dense time series, a lightweight 'legend inertia' to debounce series visibility toggles during fast pointer movement, and an ARIA-first tooltip exposure model (focus-first, aria-live updates, reduced motion). Deliverables: design tokens for series densities, interaction spec, annotated Figma components, and QA checklist for performance and screen-reader behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Pixel-binning enabled behind feature flag; reduces render calls by >= 40% for series > 10k points without visible artifacts at common zoom levels
Legend inertia implemented: rapid pointer movement will defer toggles for 150ms and show affordance; unit tests and integration tests added
Tooltips meet WCAG 2.2: keyboard focus opens tooltip, tooltip content announced via aria-live polite, reduced-motion respect via prefers-reduced-motion
Design tokens added for thinned stroke widths, min-pixel thresholds, and density breakpoints; documented in design system tokens page
Performance regression dashboard (Grafana) shows no >5% latency increase for small series (<500 points) after rollout
design_notes: Exploration found two viable binning strategies: uniform pixel-binning (aggregate by X-pixel) and adaptive LTTB-style sampling. Chose pixel-binning for predictable error bounds and easier GPU/CPU split.
Legend inertia: 150ms debounce with visual micro-affordance (ghost outline) to make it discoverable. This avoids repeated show/hide thrash when pointer crosses legend during scrubbing.

Tooltip exposure: default behavior is 'focus opens, hover previews'. On hover we show a subtle preview that is not aria-live; full tooltip becomes a focus target and its content is announced. This prevents screen readers reading every hover change.
Fallbacks: for accessibility mode or when prefers-reduced-motion is enabled, inertia is disabled and tooltips are immediate but with reduced animation.

Edge-case: stacked time-series with negative/positive spikes require min-sampling preservation; we keep peak-preservation within a bin by storing max/min alongside average for render (visual hint if peaks lost).
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose pixel-binning vs. LTTB sampling after perf workshop (engineering + design). Tradeoff: slight smoothing artifacts vs. much simpler runtime and lower CPU on continuous scrubs.
2026-03-04: Agreed on 150ms legend inertia; PM worried about discoverability so added ghost-outline affordance and tooltip hint (title: 'Hold to toggle')
2026-03-06: Accessibility review (Diego & Noor) requested keyboard-first tooltip activation and aria-live polite for content changes — accepted.
2026-03-08: Engineering flagged dependency ENG-4189 (kernel scheduling bug that increases render jitter) — blocked until mitigation or soft rollback path added.
2026-03-09: Motion-reduction path finalized: use CSS transition-duration: 0ms and disable micro-affordance motion for users with prefers-reduced-motion.
